awd_titl_txt: Conference: Support for the Workshop on Cyber Security
awd_abstract_narration:
The workshop will allows researchers to share research ideas and discuss interesting research problems. The workshop will focus on topic areas of Trustworthy AI, Resilient Networks, and others. The workshop program will include keynote speeches, lightning talks, and round-table discussions, designed to spark innovation, deepen technical exchanges, and lay the groundwork for a shared vision of cybersecurity research. By facilitating these critical interactions, the workshop aims to advance the state of the art in cybersecurity, develop a roadmap for future research collaborations, and promote long-lasting partnerships.

The proposed workshop seeks support to cover the venue facility costs and the travel expenses for invited participants from U.S. institutions to attend a research workshop in Washington, D.C., on March 3-4, 2025. By enabling in-person exchanges among leading researchers, the workshop aims to foster impactful collaborations in cybersecurity research.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This award supported an in-person cybersecurity research workshop held in Washington, D.C., on March 3–4, 2025. The workshop brought together more than 40 participants to exchange research ideas, discuss emerging cybersecurity challenges, and explore opportunities for future collaboration. The program included keynote speeches, lightning talks, and round-table discussions focused on Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence, resilient networks, and related areas of cybersecurity. These sessions encouraged participants to share new research directions, identify open technical problems and emerging research gaps, and discuss how the community can address security and resilience challenges in increasingly complex computing systems. The workshop strengthened connections among researchers working across AI, networking, systems, and security, and helped build a shared vision for future cybersecurity research. Major outcomes included the identification of promising research directions, expanded professional networks among participants, and the development of foundations for future partnerships and collaborative proposals. By supporting venue facility costs and travel expenses for invited participants, the award enabled meaningful in-person technical exchange that helped advance the cybersecurity research community. The workshop’s broader impact lies in fostering collaborations that can improve the trustworthiness, security, and resilience of computing systems used by society and benefit public, academic, and governmental stakeholders over time in lasting ways.
